claim: A .gitignore whose own rules match itself still triggers the daemon's ignore-set rebuild when edited, so filter changes take effect without a daemon restart
A running daemon does not snapshot files beneath a directory whose only .gitignore matches itself (the recording path, not just is_ignored)

unignore_is_honored_without_other_watched_activity: after a mid-run .gitignore edit that re-includes a path, a live daemon records that path with NO other watched activity in the window; the test is RED against the pre-fix daemon

maybe_rebuild_runs_once_per_dirty_flag: maybe_rebuild() returns Some exactly once for a run of consecutive dirty-flag settings and clears the flag, so a hot .gitignore cannot trigger more than one IgnoreSet::build per POLL tick
positive control precedes the ignore-rule edit in the E2E, so the test cannot be satisfied by unrelated watched activity firing the rebuild under pre-fix code

behavior under a stable ignore config is unchanged: self_ignoring_gitignore_dir_is_not_recorded_by_a_real_daemon and records_rich_turn_with_transcript_prompt_and_model_and_filters_ignored pass untouched and un-weakened
the strengthened unit test asserts its own precondition (the edited .gitignore classifies Ignore) so it cannot pass for the wrong reason
daemon_counts_ignore_rebuilds: a live daemon that reloads its ignore set once persists ignore_rebuilds:1 in state.json; a second .gitignore edit makes it 2
status_omits_reload_line_when_never_reloaded: a daemon run with no .gitignore change ends with ignore_rebuilds 0 and bare status prints no reload line at all (never a vacuous '0 reloads')
status_tolerates_state_without_rebuild_counter: a pre-existing state.json lacking the new field parses via serde default and renders as never-reloaded; status --json carries the field
rebuild_count_is_bounded_by_writes: five rapid .gitignore rewrites yield ignore_rebuilds >= 1 and <= 5, asserted on the persisted counter and never by counting stderr lines inside a timing window

SUPERSEDES clm_23B6MYA8 (whose text is false as delivered): the rebuild counter is bounded by POLL ticks, not raw events — 40 rapid .gitignore rewrites yield ignore_rebuilds in 1..=10, and the plan's literal 5-writes/1..=5 form was measured NOT to discriminate its own per-event neuter (5 writes coalesce to ~3 FSEvents notify events)

REPLACES the REFUTED clm_1H62NAJN, whose replay command was malformed by its author (two positional filters to cargo test, which accepts one, so it errored instead of running anything and never proved the property): behavior under a stable ignore config is unchanged — self_ignoring_gitignore_dir_is_not_recorded_by_a_real_daemon and records_rich_turn_with_transcript_prompt_and_model_and_filters_ignored both pass, un-weakened

replay.cmd: cargo test -p agentrec --test integration self_ignoring_gitignore_dir_is_not_recorded_by_a_real_daemon -- --exact --test-threads=3 && cargo test -p agentrec --test integration records_rich_turn_with_transcript_prompt_and_model_and_filters_ignored -- --exact --test-threads=3

claim: deleted_gitignore_rewidens_recording: deleting a .gitignore mid-run causes previously-ignored paths to be recorded on their next mutation, with no daemon restart and no unrelated watched activity
new_gitignore_honored_without_restart: a .gitignore created mid-run under a directory that had none takes effect without a daemon restart

nested_gitignore_precedence asserts its own precondition (matchers.len() >= 2) and runs in a real git repo; NO neuter is claimed for it — post-D29 IgnoreSet::build probes each directory directly, so removing git init is expected to change nothing, and this is hygiene not a vacuity fix
unignore_is_honored_without_other_watched_activity runs under SingleDaemonGuard so a RED run (which TDD and every neuter check produce by design) cannot leak a live daemon
